outerAgentProtocol: On an authorized invocation, first use the read-only status entrypoint for the exact business date. Reuse its exact run_id when present; do not create a second run for that date.
Run the public entrypoint for that exact run. Read the final compact stdout summary and the exact run-scoped workflow_handoff.json it names; do not depend on one large stdout payload.

For editorial_phase=screening, the current Automation Codex applies ai-account-editorial-director to every trusted same-run candidate and returns one candidate-local request_deep_read boolean plus substantive reason per candidate. The request is 0..N and is the only input to the existing deterministic video stage; traffic, recency, source count and persona remain evidence, not Python visibility gates. After that stage, apply the same Skill to the full pool with only the requested same-run media and write the existing final select|observe|reject|failed result. The controller never authors visible editorial fields.

Once the public entrypoint process is running, wait for that live process to exit. Do not infer a hang from artifact or file-mtime silence and do not interrupt a live process on that basis; the existing Douyin bounded tail retry may remain silent for 600000ms. The existing total automation execution boundary remains unchanged.

When waiting_stage or waiting_stage_process is returned, preserve the exact run checkpoint. A subsequent authorized invocation resumes that run. This candidate does not add wakeups or change the existing daily schedule.

When editorial is required, the current Automation Codex directly applies ai-account-editorial-director to the exact candidate batch and writes the existing simple editorial result. The controller validates and commits that result; it does not author editorial content.

For article_required, the current Automation Codex opens the active austin-voice-scriptwriter SKILL.md identified by owner_invocation and follows its existing reading order, opening the full current references and any relevant cases it calls for. Read this topic's same-run source material; file reads and first-party research tools remain available. Reference hashes or historical reads are not Skill application. Submit required_article_input as packet_id plus article via --article-item-file. For spoken_adaptation_required, open the full frozen article and spoken-adaptation.md, then submit required_spoken_adaptation_input as packet_id, article_sha256 and script via --script-item-file. Use the packet's failure envelope for item-local insufficiency. The Skill owns creative decisions; the controller owns phase order and checkpoints.

Use each public packet's phase-specific result envelope. scripts_required is a compatibility stage marker, not a request for a bare script: invoke the same public entrypoint again to obtain article_required or spoken_adaptation_required. Resume from the returned exact checkpoint until local terminal completion.

The owner-only publisher client reads its runtime-only config and attempts one terminal snapshot. Publish pending is not a business failure. Later authorized invocations return terminal noop and never repeat completed upstream stages, Skills, or an applied Website POST.
